**A.** An unlawful killing by a minister abroad is a public, sovereign act (jure imperii), not a commercial one, so it cannot be jure gestionis. The shared note is wrong: a minister's official acts are not treated as personal conduct, and foreign courts do not hear any case regardless of its nature, because a sitting minister has personal immunity (ratione personae) and official acts carry immunity ratione materiae, though whether serious international crimes lift that immunity is still contested. Immunity affects whether a court can hear the case, not how the act is classified, so A remains the best answer.

CONFIDENCE: 70
